newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A jump in South African industrial futures contracts propelled spot industrial shares higher in afternoon trading after a slow but firmer start following fresh highs on Wall Street overnight.
Golds stocks ended weaker, weighed down by bullion's recent lows, but rose off their poorest levels as the gold price clawed above the $358 level towards the local close.

The industrial index surged 61.7 points to close at 7,944.2 in tandem with the March industrial futures contract which at 1425 GMT was trading 150 points stronger at 7,800/12 from 7,640 Monday settlement.
"The industrial futures are showing signs of a good bull market," an equities trader said.
Futures traders said contracts rose as players, returning from holiday, covered short positions opened before they went on leave.
"People that were short were squeezed a bit hard. There was also some closing of reverse arbitrage positions, with people selling the futures and buying spot," a futures dealer said.
A stronger bond market and rand, which ended more than three cents firmer against the dollar, contributed to industrial stocks and futures' rise.

Dealers said industrial stocks saw some genuine buying, mainly locally based, and which appeared to be from unit trust funds. Perceptions that the market was oversold and stocks were cheap was another factor.
"On the charts, the industrial 100 index has broken below the 200-day moving average and provided an almost unique buying opportunity," a dealer said.
Amongst stocks, SAB climbed 200 cents to 117.75 rand, Nedcor rose 125 cents to 64 rand, Malbak added 25 cents to 21.25 and Sappi surged 190 cents or over 4.5 percent to 43.90.

On the gold board, stocks were largely ignored drifting down alongside bullion. Shares received a late fillip when bullion lifted above the $358 level after fixing at a fresh 3 -1/4 year low in London morning trade.
"There is not much interest on gold shares, especially with the way industrials are going up," a trader said.

The gold index finished off 9.9 points at 1,412.3, a fresh year low, with the related March futures contract at 975/93 from 993 before. Amongst stocks Vaal Reefs was off 150 cents to 285 rand, Dries lost 70 cents to 45.15 rand but Freegold was up 80 at 33 rand.
The all-share spot index ended up 37.9 points at 6,614.1 with the near month all-share contract at 6,175/97 from 6,080.
Traders said gold would track the bullion price on Wednesday and industrials were expected to extend their gains.
